verdicts.summary: A promote-to-steer after Stop rolls back completely. The cancel events emitted before dispatchSteerIntoRun fails are never returned or persisted, because events are only handed back when the command succeeds.
verdicts.scenario: Queued run Q, then Stop with holdQueue, then promote Q into the stopping run R. dispatchQueuedMessagePromoteToSteer emits run/attempt/node 'cancelled' events into the events Ref (7770-7809) before dispatchSteerIntoRun fails at 3963. I checked whether those cancel events leak: the dispatch only returns events at 11243-11244 after the switch completes, so the failure short-circuits and Q stays queued and held.

verdicts.summary: An auto send that resolves to steer or restart is downgraded to queue_after_active. The running run R still counts as blocking, so the message queues behind it. Hold handling is correct for user sends and for sends from anyone else.
verdicts.scenario: Tried three cases. (a) A non-user auto send (agent, or a scheduled task) during the Stop window: heldRunsToRelease is empty, so the new run gets queueHeld true (5172-5177) and waits for Resume, which is the intended behaviour. (b) A provider whose auto send resolves to restart_active, which would then fail ensureQueuedMessages (CommandPolicy.ts:193-197, 273-282). That needs a provider with supportsSteeringByInterruptRestart but no supportsQueuedMessages, and the only in-tree adapter with restart support also supports queued messages. (c) A delegated-completion steer after the downgrade: that is already finding 0.

verdicts.summary: stopReachedRun is true as soon as a run_interrupt_request item exists. If the provider interrupt itself fails, the run keeps running with that item, and the run can no longer be steered for the rest of its turn.
verdicts.scenario: 1. Run R is running with a live session. 2. The user presses Stop; run.interrupt persists run_interrupt_request and queues a provider-turn.interrupt effect (9589-9611). 3. session.interruptTurn fails with a retryable error (ProviderTurnControlService.ts:221). After 5 attempts the effect is failed terminally (EffectWorker.ts:760-763), and nothing in the paths I read settles R, so the provider turn keeps running. I did not trace every adapter's failure path. 4. Explicit steers and promote-to-steer into R now fail at 3963 with 'is stopping', and auto sends queue at 4825. Before this commit those steers reached the still-running agent.
verdicts.consequence: The user sees 'Target run … is stopping and cannot be steered' on a turn that is still running, until the turn ends or Stop is retried.
